description: What a Robinhood Chain token's market cap was at a past block or time, or is now, read from the chain: its price in dollars, its supply, and the two multiplied. The price is a pool's price right after the last swap at or before the block, read from that swap's log on Uniswap v3 or v4, in the deepest pool that pairs the token with USDG, which is counted as one dollar. The pools weighed are the ones that traded in the 300,000 blocks up to the block, about eight hours at ten blocks a second. When none did, the search goes back 100,000 blocks at a time, up to 3,000,000 blocks, and weighs the pools that traded in the first stretch that has a trade. When no pool paired with USDG traded there, the deepest pool paired with ETH or WETH is used, and its price is turned into dollars with ETH's price in ETH's deepest pool paired with USDG, read the same way at the same block and given as `ethUsd`. A pool's depth is `depth2pctUsd`: the dollar value of what it holds between 2% under its price and 2% over it, from its active liquidity after its last swap, with liquidity added or removed around that price since then taken into account, held across that band. Half of it is what a buy takes to move the price up 2%, and the other half what a sale takes to move it down 2%. A pool with a `depth2pctUsd` under $2,000 is marked `thin`: a $1,000 buy moves its price about 2% or more, so its price says little. A thin pool is still used when it is the deepest. The supply is what the token's Transfer logs say was minted less what was burned up to the block, since Robinhood Chain's public endpoint keeps no state that old. The tool checks the method at the newest block, where the same sum must equal the token's own totalSupply, and `supplyCheck` gives the `block` checked and whether the check `passed`. If it did not, the token's supply does not follow its Transfer logs, and no past `supply` or `marketCapUsd` is given: `supplyCheck` then gives what the `transfers` add up to and the `totalSupply`. Without a cut-off, `supply` is the token's totalSupply at the newest block. The market cap is the price times the whole supply, tokens held by the deployer or locked in a pool included. Pass the token's contract address as `token`; the `contract` of an entry from brainchain_custody_additions works. `token` can also be a symbol or name, such as RLUSD or Ripple USD, looked up on BitGo's lists for Robinhood Chain; when none there goes by it, on the lists the BrainChain MCP dataset records (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin and Gate); and when none there does either, among every token with a Uniswap pool by the symbol its contract gives itself (`pool index`). When exactly one token goes by it, `lookup` in the answer names the `contract` it stands for and its `source`, and for one found in the dataset the `dataset` day, block and manifest read; when several do, the answer lists them as `candidates`, each with its `source`, and reads nothing more. A symbol is whatever the token's deployer chose, so check the contract before relying on one found in the pool index. To read a past block, pass `atBlock`, a block number, or `at`, a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z, for the last block made at or before it. Without either, the tool reads the newest block. In the answer, `asOf` gives the `block` the figures are for and when it was made (`at`), and `readAt` when the chain was read. `priceUsd`, `supply` and `marketCapUsd` are at that block, the price as the pool stood after `swap`, the swap it comes from, with its `block`, `at` and `transaction`. `pool` is the pool used: its `version`, its `address` on Uniswap v3 or its `id` on Uniswap v4 with its `hooks`, the `pair`, `pairedWith`, the other token's contract address or ETH, its `fee`, its `depth2pctUsd` at the block and `thin`. `chosen` says why that pool, and `pools` lists the pools it was weighed against, deepest first, each with its last swap's `block` and its `priceUsd` and `depth2pctUsd`. `token` holds the `contract` and the `name`, `symbol` and `decimals` the contract gives itself. Anyone can create a pool for any token and trade in it, and whoever deployed a token chose its name, symbol and supply, so a price from a thin pool, or for a token whose origin you do not know, proves little. The token's pools, and ETH's, come from the pool index of the watcher BRAINCHAIN_WATCH_URL names, BrainChain's own by default, when it answers within 3 seconds; the blocks after the index are searched on chain, and `poolIndex` then gives the `watcher` and the block the index ran `through`. A pool from the index counts only when its address or id follows from its own currencies and fee, and the prices, liquidity and supply are always read from the chain. When the watcher does not answer, the tool searches the chain for every pool created for the token, and `poolIndex` is left out. The tool answers one request at a time, in turn with the other tools that read the chain. The first answer for a token can take half a minute when it searches for the pools itself, or about ten seconds with the index; later ones are faster for as long as the server keeps running. An answer that is not ready after 45 seconds says so, and asking again goes on from where it stopped. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

at.description: Optional, in place of atBlock: a time in ISO 8601, such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z. The figures are those at the last block made at or before it.

atBlock.description: Optional: a block number. The figures are those at the end of that block.

token.description: The token's contract address on Robinhood Chain, 0x followed by 40 hex characters, or its symbol or name, such as RLUSD.

name: brainchain_token_market_cap
title: A Robinhood Chain token's market cap at a past block or time
